ayasofya: A vast domed building completed in 537; used as a church, mosque and museum, open today as a mosque.
Tram T1 to Sultanahmet, then a 3-minute walk.
mavi: A 17th-century mosque with six minarets, famous for the blue İznik tiles inside.
topkapi: The palace Ottoman sultans ruled from for about four centuries; courtyards, the Harem and Bosphorus views.
Tram T1, Sultanahmet or Gülhane stop.
yerebatan: A 6th-century underground cistern known for its forest of columns and the Medusa-head column bases.
Tram T1, Sultanahmet stop; very close to Hagia Sophia.
kapalicarsi: One of the oldest and largest covered markets in the world; carpets, ceramics, leather and jewelry shops.
misir: A 17th-century bazaar selling spices, Turkish delight, nuts and tea, right next to the New Mosque.
suleymaniye: Mimar Sinan's 16th-century mosque complex; its courtyard looks over the Golden Horn and the city.
Walk uphill from Eminönü or Beyazıt, about 15 minutes.
galatakulesi: A 14th-century stone tower; its upper terrace gives a wide view of the old city and the Golden Horn.
Metro M2, Şişhane stop; or walk uphill from Karaköy.
galatakoprusu: Links the two banks of the Golden Horn; anglers on top, restaurants below. Lovely for a sunset walk.
Tram T1, Karaköy or Eminönü stop.
taksim: Shops, cafés, the nostalgic tram and restaurants in the side streets; the city's busiest pedestrian street.
dolmabahce: A grand 19th-century palace on the Bosphorus, known for its ceremonial hall with a crystal chandelier.
Tram T1 to Kabataş, then a 15-minute walk.
ortakoy: A lively neighborhood below the Bosphorus Bridge with a waterfront mosque, cafés and kumpir stalls.
Bus from Kabataş or Beşiktaş; you can also walk along the shore.
kizkulesi: A tower on a tiny island off Üsküdar; one of Istanbul's symbols, with legends and Bosphorus views.
By boat from Üsküdar or Salacak.
beylerbeyi: A 19th-century summer palace on the Asian shore of the Bosphorus; the gardens are open too.
Bus or minibus from Üsküdar; also seen on Bosphorus cruises.
rumelihisari: A Bosphorus fortress built in a few months in 1452 by Mehmed the Conqueror; you can walk on the walls.
Bus to Rumelihisarı stop; or a shore walk from Bebek.
pierreloti: A hilltop tea garden and viewing terrace over the Golden Horn; reached by cable car from Eyüp.
Cable car or uphill walk from Eyüp Sultan.
kadikoy: The lively market streets, cafés and Moda seafront of the Asian side; great for eating out.
About 25 minutes by ferry from Eminönü or Karaköy.
fenerbalat: Colorful historic houses, the Greek Patriarchate and the Bulgarian Church on the Golden Horn; popular for photos.
Golden Horn ferry or bus from Eminönü to Fener or Balat.
kariye: The Byzantine Chora Monastery, famous for its mosaics and frescoes; open today as a mosque.
About a 15-minute uphill walk from Balat.
eyup: One of Istanbul's most visited mosques, with the tomb of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari and a historic market around it.
Golden Horn ferry or bus from Eminönü to Eyüpsultan.
rahmikoc: A museum of transport, industry and communication on the Golden Horn; submarine, trains and aircraft.
miniaturk: An open-air museum of miniature models of famous buildings from Türkiye and Ottoman lands.
On the Golden Horn; by bus or Golden Horn ferry.
bozdogan: A 4th-century Roman aqueduct that spans Atatürk Boulevard.
Metro M2, a short walk from Vezneciler.
hipodrom: The Byzantine chariot-racing ground; home to the Obelisk, the Serpent Column and the German Fountain.
arkeoloji: A three-building museum in the outer gardens of Topkapı Palace, known for the Alexander Sarcophagus.
rustempasa: Mimar Sinan's small mosque covered inside with İznik tiles; right by the Spice Bazaar.
pera: An art museum whose collection includes Osman Hamdi Bey's The Tortoise Trainer; near İstiklal Street.
Metro M2, a short walk from Şişhane.
istanbulmodern: A contemporary art museum on the Bosphorus, in a new building designed by Renzo Piano.
yildiz: A former palace grove; tree-lined paths and pavilions make it a quiet break in the city.
A short walk from Beşiktaş toward Ortaköy.
bebek: A Bosphorus neighborhood known for its bay, waterfront promenade and cafés; walking distance to Rumeli Fortress.
Coastal buses from Kabataş or Beşiktaş.
mihrimah: Mimar Sinan's mosque facing the Üsküdar pier; also called the Pier Mosque.
kuzguncuk: A quiet Bosphorus neighborhood of wooden houses, with a mosque, church and synagogue side by side.
Bus from Üsküdar or about a 20-minute shore walk.
kucuksu: A 19th-century hunting pavilion on the Asian shore of the Bosphorus, known for its ornate facade.
selimiye: The 16th-century mosque Mimar Sinan called his masterpiece; UNESCO World Heritage.
bursaulu: With its twenty domes, one of the best-known examples of early Ottoman architecture.
bursayesil: A 15th-century mosque and tomb famous for their turquoise tiles.
truva: The ancient city linked with Homer's Iliad; UNESCO World Heritage.
assos: An ancient harbor village on the Aegean with the ruins of the Temple of Athena and stone houses.
cunda: An island across from Ayvalık known for stone streets, fish restaurants and sunsets.
sapanca: A freshwater lake ringed by walking paths and cafés.
efes: One of the great cities of the ancient world, famous for the Library of Celsus and its great theater; UNESCO World Heritage.
izmirsaat: İzmir's 1901 clock tower, the city's symbol, and the historic Kemeraltı Bazaar next to it.
alacati: A Çeşme town known for stone houses, boutique cafés and windsurfing.
bergama: The ancient city of Pergamon with its steep theater and Temple of Trajan; UNESCO World Heritage.
pamukkale: White travertine terraces with the ancient city of Hierapolis above; UNESCO World Heritage.
afrodisias: An ancient city known for its sculpture school, stadium and Tetrapylon gate; UNESCO World Heritage.
didim: One of antiquity's major oracle sites, with the giant columns of the Temple of Apollo.
bodrum: A 15th-century Crusader castle over the harbor, home to the Museum of Underwater Archaeology.
oludeniz: A beach known for its turquoise lagoon and paragliding flights from Babadağ.
marmaris: A resort town known for its marina and boat trips to the nearby bays.
datca: Quiet bays on a peninsula between the Aegean and Mediterranean, with ancient Knidos at the tip.
dalyan: Royal rock tombs, a reed-lined channel and İztuzu Beach, where loggerhead turtles nest.
kaleici: The walled old town; narrow streets, Hadrian's Gate and the historic harbor.
aspendos: A Roman-era theater, one of the best preserved in the world.
side: A historic peninsula with the seaside columns of the Temple of Apollo and an ancient theater.
alanya: A Seljuk castle on top of the peninsula, with the Red Tower and shipyard below.
kas: A harbor town facing the Greek island of Kastellorizo; known for diving and Kekova boat trips.
termessos: An ancient city on a mountainside, said to have resisted Alexander the Great.
kizkalesi: Famous for its castle in the sea just off the beach; the ruins of Korykos Castle stand opposite.
salda: A protected lake called Türkiye's Maldives for its turquoise water and white shores.
sagalassos: An ancient city at about 1,500 meters in the Taurus Mountains, known for its monumental fountain.
anitkabir: The mausoleum of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk; the Road of Lions, ceremonial square and museum.
anadolumed: A museum of Anatolian civilizations, especially Hittite and Phrygian works; next to Ankara Castle.
goreme: Rock-cut Byzantine churches decorated with frescoes; UNESCO World Heritage.
uchisar: A rock castle at one of Cappadocia's highest points, with views over the region.
derinkuyu: A multi-level underground city connected by narrow passages.
ihlara: A deep canyon with a walking trail along the Melendiz stream and rock-cut churches.
mevlana: The tomb of Mevlana Jalaluddin Rumi, known for its conical dome of green tiles.
catalhoyuk: A Neolithic settlement dating back 9,000 years; UNESCO World Heritage.
odunpazari: A walkable historic quarter of Ottoman wooden houses, galleries and cafés.
divrigi: A 13th-century mosque and hospital famous for its stone carving; UNESCO World Heritage.
sumela: A Byzantine monastery built into a sheer cliff in the Altındere Valley.
uzungol: A lake ringed by mountains, wooden houses and walking paths; one of the Black Sea's best-known stops.
ayder: A highland plateau at the foot of the Kaçkar Mountains, with hot springs and hiking routes.
safranbolu: A town of Ottoman mansions and an old bazaar on the UNESCO World Heritage list.
amasra: A small Black Sea town with two bays and a castle; known for fish restaurants.
amasya: Historic houses on the Yeşilırmak river and Pontic royal rock tombs on the cliff above.
hattusa: The Hittite capital; the Lion Gate and nearby Yazılıkaya; UNESCO World Heritage.
abant: A lake surrounded by pine forest, with a walking and cycling path around it.
ani: A medieval city on the Arpaçay river with ruins of churches, a mosque and walls; UNESCO World Heritage.
akdamar: A 10th-century church of the Holy Cross on an island in Lake Van, famous for its reliefs.
vankalesi: A rock fortress from the Urartian period; sunsets over Lake Van.
ishakpasa: A 17th-18th-century palace near Doğubayazıt facing Mount Ararat, rich in stone carving.
ciftemin: A 13th-century madrasa, Erzurum's symbol, with a carved stone portal and twin minarets.
nemrutkrater: A huge volcanic crater with lakes inside, near Tatvan.
gobeklitepe: A temple site over 11,000 years old known for its T-shaped pillars; UNESCO World Heritage.
balikligol: The heart of the city, with sacred fish and the mosques and madrasas around the pool.
harran: A historic settlement known for beehive-shaped mud-brick houses and the ruins of an ancient university.
mardin: A historic city of stone houses, madrasas and terraces over the Mesopotamian plain.
diyarbakir: One of the longest city walls in the world and the Hevsel Gardens; UNESCO World Heritage.
nemrutdagi: King Antiochus's tumulus with giant stone heads; people climb it for sunrise; UNESCO World Heritage.
gaziantep: The coppersmiths' bazaar around the castle and the city's famous cuisine make for a great visit.
buyukada: The largest of the Princes' Islands; mansions, pine woods and quiet roads you can cycle.
By ferry from Kabataş or Bostancı.
cumalikizik: A preserved Ottoman village of stone and timber houses, famous for village breakfasts; UNESCO World Heritage.
uludag: A mountain for skiing in winter and hiking and picnics in summer; reached by cable car from Bursa.
gelibolu: The site of the 1915 Gallipoli battles; memorials, cemeteries and a visitor center.
bozcaada: A small Aegean island with a castle, vineyards and a colorful old quarter of narrow streets.
igneada: Rare floodplain forests and lakes on the Black Sea coast; a national park.
yalovatermal: Hot springs in a wooded valley, in use since Roman times.
sardes: The capital of the Lydian Kingdom; Temple of Artemis, gymnasium and an ancient synagogue.
aizanoi: An ancient city at Çavdarhisar with one of Anatolia's best-preserved temples of Zeus.
afyonkale: A castle on a rock rising from the city center, reached by a long staircase.
foca: A quiet coastal town with stone houses, a fishing harbor and bays where Mediterranean monk seals live.
priene: An ancient hillside city with a grid of streets and the Temple of Athena.
laodikya: A large ancient city still being excavated, with colonnaded streets and two theaters; near Pamukkale.
saklikent: A narrow, deep canyon you walk through in icy water; a place to cool off in summer.
akyaka: A quiet town on the Gulf of Gökova with wooden houses, the clear Azmak river and a windy beach.
egirdir: A town on a small peninsula reaching into the lake; known for sunsets and lake fish.
olimpos: Ancient ruins in the forest, a long pebble beach and the eternal flames of Yanartaş nearby.
myra: Lycian rock tombs, an ancient theater and the nearby Church of St. Nicholas.
duden: A waterfall that drops off the cliffs straight into the sea at Lara; best seen from its park.
patara: An ancient city with a beach that runs for kilometers and the assembly hall of the Lycian League.
cennetobrugu: Huge sinkholes near Silifke; a small chapel stands at the bottom of the Heaven sinkhole.
tasköprü: A Roman-era stone bridge over the Seyhan river, still in use.
gordion: The Phrygian capital near Polatlı, with the Midas Mound and a museum; UNESCO World Heritage.
esrefoglu: A 13th-century mosque in Beyşehir with wooden columns; UNESCO World Heritage.
avanos: A Cappadocian town on the Kızılırmak river known for its pottery workshops.
erciyes: Central Anatolia's highest mountain, with a ski resort on its slopes.
trabzonayasofya: A 13th-century Byzantine church on a hill above the sea, known for its frescoes; open today as a mosque.
yedigoller: Seven forest lakes linked by streams, famous for their autumn colors.
sinopcezaevi: A former prison inside the city walls, now visited as a museum.
kastamonukale: A castle above the city, best visited together with the old bazaar and mansions below.
giresunadasi: The only island in the eastern Black Sea; reached by boat and known for legends and seabird colonies.
boztepe: A viewpoint over Ordu and the Black Sea, reached by cable car from the city.
cildir: A high plateau lake where horse-drawn sleigh rides cross the frozen surface in winter.
agridagi: Türkiye's highest mountain; summit climbs need a permit and a guide.
palandoken: A ski resort right next to Erzurum, known for its long runs.
harput: A historic settlement above Elazığ with a castle, a great mosque and a leaning minaret.
arslantepe: A mound whose layers shed light on the rise of early states; UNESCO World Heritage.
midyat: A historic town of stone mansions and filigree silversmiths, with Syriac monasteries nearby.
dara: A Roman frontier city with rock-cut tombs and underground cisterns.
